AL.reason: The corpus is Alabama Code Chapter 34-37, which is the Plumbers and Gas Fitters licensing law that directly regulates master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

AR.reason: The corpus is Arkansas Code Title 17 Chapter 38 which directly licenses and regulates master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and restricted plumbers in Arkansas.

AZ.reason: The corpus is ARS Chapter 10 (Title 32, Article 1 et seq.) which is Arizona's Registrar of Contractors statute that licenses all contractor classifications including specialty plumbing contractors, covering definitions, qualifications, licensing, fees, and enforcement.

CA.reason: The corpus is California's Contractors State License Law (Business and Professions Code Chapter 9, sections 7000 et seq.), which licenses all contractor classifications including plumbing contractors under the specialty contractor provisions of this chapter.

CO.reason: The corpus contains Colorado Article 155 (Plumbers), which directly licenses master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, residential plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

CT.reason: The corpus contains Connecticut Chapter 393 sections explicitly defining plumbing and piping work, establishing the Plumbing and Piping Work examining board, and setting licensure requirements for plumbing contractors and journeymen.

DE.reason: The corpus contains the Delaware Board of Plumbing, Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Examiners chapter, which explicitly licenses master plumbers including requirements, examinations, fees, discipline, and enforcement under §§ 1807-1817.

FL.reason: The corpus contains Florida Chapter 489 which explicitly licenses plumbing contractors (defined in s. 489.105, referenced in s. 489.107(2)(h), and specifically regulated in s. 489.1136 regarding medical gas certification for plumbing contractors).

GA.reason: The corpus is Georgia Code Chapter 43-14, which explicitly licenses master plumbers and journeyman plumbers through the Division of Master Plumbers and Journeyman Plumbers, including examination, licensing requirements, and prohibitions on unlicensed practice.

HI.reason: Hawaii Chapter 448E explicitly licenses and regulates journey worker plumbers and master plumbers, including definitions, qualifications, board powers, renewal requirements, and unlicensed activity prohibitions.

IA.reason: Iowa Code Chapter 105 is explicitly titled the Iowa Plumber, Mechanical Professional, and Contractor Licensing Act and contains licensure requirements for journeyperson plumbers, master plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

ID.reason: The corpus contains Idaho Code Title 54 Chapter 26, which is the Idaho plumbing licensing law explicitly regulating plumbing contractors, journeyman plumbers, and apprentice plumbers including examination, certification, fees, and board administration.

IL.reason: The corpus is the Illinois Plumbing License Law (225 ILCS 320) which directly licenses plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

IN.reason: The corpus contains Indiana Code Title 25 Article 28.5 which is explicitly the plumbers licensing chapter covering plumbing contractors and journeyman plumbers including licensing requirements, examinations, renewals, and the plumbers recovery fund.

KY.reason: Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 318 directly licenses and regulates master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, and plumbing contractors, including definitions, license requirements, examinations, fees, renewal, and revocation.

LA.reason: The corpus contains Louisiana RS 37:1361-1380, which is the State Plumbing Board chapter directly licensing master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, residential plumbers limited, and related plumbing occupations.

MA.reason: The corpus is Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 142 (Supervision of Plumbing), which directly licenses and regulates master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and master/journeyman gas fitters.

MD.reason: The corpus contains Maryland GBO Title 12, which is the State plumbing licensing law establishing the State Board of Plumbing and setting out licensure requirements for master plumbers, journey plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and related occupations.

ME.reason: The corpus contains Maine's Plumbers Examining Board statutes (32 M.R.S. ch. 131) defining master plumber, journeyman plumber, licensing requirements, examinations, and renewals for plumbers.

MI.reason: The corpus is Michigan's Skilled Trades Regulation Act (MCL 339.5101–339.6133), which explicitly covers plumbing licensure including the state plumbing board and plumber/plumbing contractor licensing requirements under its articles.

MN.reason: Chapter 326B contains Minnesota's unified construction codes and licensing statute, which explicitly covers plumbing licensure (master plumber, journeyman plumber, plumbing contractor) among other trades regulated under this chapter.

MO.reason: RSMo Chapter 341 explicitly licenses master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, and plumbing contractors, covering examination, certification, bonding, and enforcement requirements.

MT.reason: MCA Title 37 Chapter 69 explicitly licenses master plumbers and journeyman plumbers in Montana, covering definitions, qualifications, examinations, and disciplinary provisions for plumbers.

NC.reason: The corpus contains NC General Statutes Chapter 87, Article 2 (Plumbing and Heating Contractors), which directly establishes the licensing board, examination, fees, and requirements for plumbing contractors in North Carolina.

ND.reason: Chapter 43-18 is the North Dakota plumbing licensure law, covering the state board of plumbing, licensing requirements for master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, and apprentices, examinations, fees, renewals, and penalties.

NH.reason: All sections in Chapter 330 (Plumbers) have been repealed, leaving no operative licensure text.

NJ.reason: The corpus is NJ Title 45:14C, the State Plumbing License Law of 1968, which directly licenses master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

NM.reason: The corpus is the New Mexico Construction Industries Licensing Act (Chapter 60, Article 13), which explicitly covers licensing of plumbing contractors and plumbers as part of the construction trades it regulates.

NV.reason: NRS Chapter 624 is Nevada's contractors licensing law that explicitly covers specialty contractors including plumbing contractors, with NRS 624.215 specifically referencing plumbing as a specialty requiring a separate license.

OH.reason: This chapter covers plumbing inspection, permits, and inspector certification by the division of industrial compliance, but does not contain licensure law for plumbers or plumbing contractors (i.e., no provisions for licensing master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, or plumbing contractors).

OK.reason: The corpus contains the Construction Industries Board Act and The Plumbing License Law of 1955 sections (59-1001 through 59-1023.1) which directly license and regulate plumbers, journeyman plumbers, and plumbing contractors in Oklahoma.

OR.reason: ORS chapter 693 directly licenses journeyman plumbers and plumbing contractors in Oregon, covering definitions, license requirements, examinations, fees, and enforcement.

RI.reason: The corpus is R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 5-20, explicitly titled the Rhode Island Plumbing License Law, and contains the full licensure framework for master plumbers, journeyperson plumbers, apprentice plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

SC.reason: The corpus is SC Title 40 Chapter 49 which directly licenses master plumbers, employing plumbers, and journeyman plumbers, requiring certificates and examinations for installing sanitary plumbing.

SD.reason: The corpus is SD Chapter 36-25 which directly establishes the State Plumbing Commission and licenses plumbers, plumbing contractors, journeyman plumbers, and apprentice plumbers.

TX.reason: The corpus is Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1301, titled Plumbers, which is the Plumbing License Law directly licensing master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, plumbing contractors, and related occupations in Texas.

UT.reason: The corpus is Utah Code Chapter 58-55 (Utah Construction Trades Licensing Act) which explicitly licenses journeyman plumbers, master plumbers, apprentice plumbers, general plumbing contractors, residential plumbing contractors, and residential master/journeyman plumbers.

VA.reason: The corpus is Virginia Code Chapter 11 of Title 54.1 (Board for Contractors), which explicitly licenses plumbing contractors as a classification (e.g., § 54.1-1100 requires a master tradesman license for plumbing contractors, § 54.1-1102 includes a licensed plumbing contractor on the Board, and § 54.1-1108.2 lists plumbing contractor as a Class C license classification).

VT.reason: The corpus contains Vermont's plumber licensing statute (26 V.S.A. Chapter 51) including definitions of master plumber and journeyman plumber, the Plumber's Examining Board, examination and licensing requirements, fees, and penalties for unlicensed practice.

WA.reason: The corpus is RCW chapter 18.106, Washington's plumber licensing statute, which directly governs journey level plumbers, specialty plumbers, residential service plumbers, and plumbing contractors.

WI.reason: Chapter 145 explicitly licenses master plumbers, journeyman plumbers, plumbing contractors, and related classifications throughout its sections.
